title: Proposal: Image Preview for HTML Images (`preview` attribute)

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

labels.name: agenda+
labels.description: To be discussed at a triage meeting

body: ### What problem are you trying to solve? Displaying lightweight image previews while full-resolution images load is a common technique for improving perceived loading performance, particularly on image-heavy pages and slow networks. However, HTML does not provide a native mechanism for managing the preview-to-final-image lifecycle. Developers must implement this themselves, adding complexity and duplicating functionality across websites. ### What solutions exist today? Developers use low-quality image placeholders (LQIP), BlurHash, ThumbHash, CSS backgrounds, canvas, and JavaScript to display previews and replace them with final images. These solutions require custom markup and logic to coordinate loading, decoding, replacement, and source changes. ### How would you solve it? We propose introducing a `preview` attribute on the HTML `` element: ```html ``` The browser would manage displaying the preview and replacing it when the final image is ready, without delaying the final image or changing existing image semantics. The proposal also explores optional capabilities, including compact preview formats and customizable transitions. See the [Image Preview explainer](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/ImagePreview/explainer.md) for details. ### Anything else? _No response_
